description.narrative: A higher degree of involvement of women in politics at local level through improving and strengthening the capacity of selected ITP candidates

ICLD ämnar fortsätta med det nationella utbildningsprogrammet: Local Leaders Capacitating Women in Zimbabwe 2015-2018. Syftet med programmet är att stärka kvinnors politiska deltagande, särskilt på lokal nivå. Programmet riktar sig till valda kvinnliga politiker som har potential att driva förändring men också agera som förebilder i det politiska livet. ICLD föreslår 50 deltagare men också 20 manliga politiker. Den utvärdering som genomförts visar att programmet har visat viktiga resultat och lagt grunden för ett fortsatt expanderat program

Support to local Government sector with Zimbabwe specific ITP course in partnership with ICDL, with the aim of promoting a higher degree of involvement of women in local politics in Zimbabwe through training workshops and exchange visits. Continuation of contribution 52120078

Forty-Six Councilors, twenty-three council managers, and five Ministry of Local Government officials were capacitated in the two 18-month programmes from late 2015 to August 2018. Seventy-four decision-makers spread across all the provinces within Zimbabwe were capable of leading their communities, making decisions that include more stakeholders- especially women- in a more efficient manner than prior to this programme. The programme has led to changes in individual’s competencies and attitudes through education and exposure to new ideas, culture, and perspectives. All the councilors expressed boosts in self confidence levels when compared to the beginning of the programme. The councilors have become bolder when speaking at public gatherings, interrogate and articulate issues better in council meetings and facilitate ward activities better. The increased confidence has not gone unnoticed for some of the participants who have now been elevated in their respective portfolios. The growth in personal confidence has also transformed other facets of the councilors’ lives as they continue to develop into community role models. This has also come with improvements in some of the councilors’ personal grooming standards as they now dress more appropriately for different occasions. The councillors gained knowledge of advocacy, lobbying and strategic planning helped them to become better communicators and negotiators. It has made their work easier as they are able to effectively negotiate with colleagues to support their views and ideas during debates. The inclusion of men into the programme has assisted in making men appreciate the challenges women face when doing council buisness.
